rationale: Description: 'Puddle of hydraulic fluid forming under the main reservoir.' (Requires inferring fluid leaks are mechanical/fluid-power issues).
Description: 'Drive unit trips after 20 minutes of operation. Motor casing unusually hot.' (Tripping and heat imply electrical overload).
Description: 'SCADA screen showing erratic jumping values for cooling water flow, but physical flow looks steady.' (Points to a faulty sensor/transmitter, not the physical pump).
Description: 'Loud whining noise coming from the drive end of the conveyor.' (Whining at a drive end implies bearing or gearbox mechanical failure).
Description: 'Acrid burning smell near the MCC panel when Line 2 starts.' (Burning smell near a control center is a classic electrical fault).
Description: 'Press won't reach full tonnage. Drifts down when held under load.' (Implies a mechanical/hydraulic bypass or seal leak).
Description: 'Robot arm moving past its home limit switch without stopping.' (Limit switch failure is an instrumentation/control issue).
Description: 'Air line hissing near the packaging cell.' (Pneumatic leaks typically route to general/facilities unless severe).
Scheduled vibration inspection on a centrifugal pump bearing train.
Motor casing heat is isolated from the separate pump-vibration complaint.
A VFD overcurrent trip points to the drive and power-control domain.
The process gauge is stable while the transmitter indication jumps.
No power reaches the CNC main control panel.
Conveyor slip under load indicates a belt or drive-train problem.
A snapped proximity device is a discrete sensing failure rather than belt damage.
The repeated VFD overcurrent event concerns the electronic drive.
A chilled-water pump leak localizes to the pump sealing or fluid path.
Cooling-water leakage is a mechanical seal or piping symptom.
A hot compressor with cooling contamination needs machine-side diagnosis despite the temperature wording.
The requested 6205 bearing is a rotating-equipment repair.
Routine CNC way-oil top-up is a general planned-maintenance task.
A snapped grid coupling is a mechanical power-transmission failure.
The conveyor stopping function depends on the failed limit sensing device.
A seized conveyor roller and scraping sound indicate bearing or roller mechanics.
The pump motor overheating finding is separate from a bearing-vibration finding.
Belt slipping under load is a conveyor mechanical condition.
The CP-401 motor heat event is an electrical motor condition.
A seized roller is not resolved by the nearby conveyor control hardware.
Elevated vibration on the standby pump indicates rotating-equipment degradation.
A mechanical seal leak on a centrifugal pump is a fluid-mechanical repair.
